record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Over the one-dimensional Euclidean space R with its usual metric, MT has a decidable satisfiability problem. Is there a transparent axiomatisation of the valid MT formulas over R, and what is the computational complexity of MT satisfiability over R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the modal logic MT with two unary modal operators interpreted on metric spaces as follows. For a metric space (X,d), an MT-model is a valuation V assigning to each propositional variable a subset of X. The language extends propositional logic with:
- a "distance" operator ◇^a, for each positive rational a, with semantics: x ⊨ ◇^a φ iff there exists y ∈ X with d(x,y) < a and y ⊨ φ;
- a topological "closure/interior" modality based on the metric topology.
(More generally MT may be taken as the natural combined modal language for metric and topology in which formulas are built from propositional variables using Boolean connectives, the parameterised distance modalities ◇^a (a ∈ ℚ_{>0}), and the topological closure modality, interpreted in metric spaces in the standard way.)

A formula is MT-valid over the real line if it is true at every point of every MT-model based on (ℝ, |·|) with the usual Euclidean metric. It is known that the satisfiability problem for MT over (ℝ, |·|) is decidable.

(a) Provide a transparent (e.g., finite or otherwise perspicuous recursive) axiomatisation of the set of MT-formulas valid in every MT-model based on the one-dimensional Euclidean space (ℝ, |·|).

(b) Determine the exact computational complexity of the satisfiability problem for MT over (ℝ, |·|).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on modal logics of metric spaces. While decidability of MT-satisfiability over ℝ is known, no transparent axiomatisation and no tight complexity bound for MT over the real line appear in the available sources; related results axiomatise only the pure topological fragment (which coincides over ℝ with S4 and is PSpace-complete) or treat distance fragments without topology. No subsequent work resolving both axiomatisation and exact complexity of full MT over ℝ was located.

status_evidence.title: Modal Logics of Metric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The modal logic of an arbitrary metric space is finitely axiomatizable, has the finite model property, and hence is decidable.
status_evidence.claim: General axiomatisation results exist for arbitrary metric spaces but not specifically a transparent axiomatisation of MT over ℝ with tight complexity.

status_evidence.title: A logic for metric and topology
status_evidence.snippet: finite axiomatisation of the logic and ... EXPTIME-completeness
status_evidence.claim: Related combined metric–topological logics have EXPTIME-complete satisfiability and finite axiomatisations over general metric spaces, but the specific case of ℝ for MT is not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Modal Logics for Metric Spaces: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems list including axiomatisation and complexity of MT over ℝ.
status_evidence.claim: Listed explicitly as an open problem.
